title: Ibn Khaldun Amazigh (Berbers) & Sudanese/Nubian Noahic Lineages

nodes.name: Berr → Bernes (Branes: Sanhaja, Masmuda, Kutama, Auréba) & Madghis al-Abtar (Botr: Zenata, Luwata, Hawwara)
nodes.era: Maghreb Tribal Origins (Ibn Khaldun Vol. 3 pp. 189-191)
nodes.role: Two Great Amazigh Branches Descended from Canaan b. Ham / Mazigh
sources: Ibn Khaldun Histoire des Berbères Vol. 1, 3 & 4
nodes.notes: Ibn Khaldun transmits the Berber genealogies dividing the Imazighen into the Branes (Sanhaja, Masmuda, Kutama, Auréba) and Botr / Madghis al-Abtar (Zenata, Luwata, Hawwara, Nefzaoua), explicitly preserving Ibn Hazm's chain tracing Madghis through Ber -> Herik -> Bedian -> Canaan -> Ham -> Noah.

nodes.name: Koceila (Auréba) & Queen al-Kahina / Dihya (Jerawa Zenata, 7th c. CE)
nodes.role: Sovereign Amazigh Leaders Descended from Branes & Botr
sources: Ibn Khaldun Histoire des Berbères Vol. 3 p. 193
nodes.notes: Koceila (leader of the Branes Auréba) and Queen al-Kahina / Dihya (queen of the Botr Jerawa Zenata confederation) led the Amazigh resistance across North Africa.

nodes.name: Nubians (Nuba) & Beja (Blemmyes) — Christian Kingdoms of Nobatia, Makuria & Alodia
nodes.era: Ancient to Medieval Sudan (MacMichael Vol. 1 pp. 12-51; Arkell)
nodes.role: Cushitic/Nubian Lineages of the Middle Nile
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan pp. 12-51
nodes.notes: Documents the pre-Islamic Cushite/Nubian and Beja populations (Blemmyes) of Northern Sudan who formed the Christian kingdoms of Nobatia, Makuria (Dongola) & Alodia (Soba).

nodes.name: Ja'aliyyin Confederation of Sudan (Descent from al-'Abbas b. 'Abd al-Muttalib → Ishmael)
nodes.role: Sudanese 'Abbasid Nisba Lineages Blended with Nubia
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan Vol. 1 pp. xi, 131-195
nodes.notes: MacMichael catalogs dozens of Sudanese Arab nisba manuscripts uniting the Ja'aliyyin, Danagla, Shayqiya, Batahin & Rubatab via Ibrahim Ja'al back to al-'Abbas, uncle of Prophet Muhammad (Quraysh/Ishmael), while intermarrying with Nubian princesses.

nodes.name: Juhayna (Guhayna), Baqqara, Kababish & Shukriya of Sudan & Kordofan (Qahtan / Joktan Line)
nodes.role: Yemenite Qahtanite Migrations via Egypt & Red Sea into Sudan
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan pp. 131, 271-319
nodes.notes: Sudanese chronicles trace the Juhayna/Guhayna confederation (Baqqara, Kababish, Shukriya, Hamar, Rizayqat) back to southern Arabian Himyar & Qahtan (Joktan), migrating through Egypt and the Red Sea into Kordofan & Darfur.

nodes.name: Funj Sultanate of Sennar (1504–1821 CE — Umayyad / Nubian Pedigree)
nodes.role: Black Sultanate of Sudan Linking Umayyad & Nubian Royal Traditions
sources: MacMichael History of Arabs in Sudan
nodes.notes: Amara Dunqas founded the Funj Sultanate at Sennar in 1504 CE; Funj royal genealogies claimed descent from Umayyad refugees passing through Abyssinia and Nubia.
